what: When the pointer enters a list row, a gray tile covers the row from the nearest edge the pointer came in from (top, bottom, left or right) over .5s cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1), and the text slides 2.5em to the right on the same curve. On exit the tile leaves toward the exit side — enter from the top and exit at the bottom, and the tile comes down from the top and passes out through the bottom.

options.axis: all (default — all four edges) · y (top and bottom only) · x (left and right only)
options.push: 0 means the text is not pushed
options.--fx-tile·--fx-push: Tile color and text shift (CSS variable), default --kf-surface · 2.5em
options.[data-fx-part=tile]: Covering tiles (children, required — nothing is applied without them)
options.dur: Entrance duration (seconds) — if given, replaces the CSS default .5s. The Name site uses .6
options.ease: Entry curve like 0.215,0.61,0.355,1 or a CSS curve name, default 0.16,1,0.3,1
options.out: Exit duration (seconds), default dur — .5 on the Name site
options.outEase: Exit curve, default ease — the source site uses power2.inOut(0.455,0.03,0.515,0.955)
options.fade: When true, tiles fade while leaving (they come in at full strength right away)
options.gap: Gap (px) that pushes hidden tiles further outside the edge, default 2 — set to 0 if the original enters exactly from 100% (corner-news-typewriter-association)

note: Not applied on touch devices (hover false). Leaving the current page row covering the tile (transform none) makes it stand like the original.

from.where: shared.js directional() footer big link row (original data-directional-hover: tile --grey #1d1d1d, text padding-left 2.5em .5s)
